To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of a water quality model for the management of the water system of a large city requires: (a) a high level of integration of ecological and social processes, (b) the use of leanification methods to reduce the complexity of the system to be modeled, and (c) the use of a probabilistic approach to describe the relations between variables.
the integration and leanification of water quality and ecological modeling can be combined to achieve models that are more convenient for water management.

the integration of more processes in ecological models is a good strategy to increase their relevance and applicability, and that leanification can be an important strategy to increase the applicability of models by reducing the time needed for model development and application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing, testing, and applying integrated, lean ecological water systems models for environmental management.
the development of ecological water system models that are relevant and applicable to support decision making and management of water systems.
the development of a modeling framework for the simulation of the dynamics in ecological water systems, which is based on the integration and leanification of the processes and variables involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integration of ecological processes in water systems models is not only a matter of increasing the level of integration, but also of finding a good balance between integration and leanification.
there is no one single best model, but that the best model is the one that is best for the specific purpose.

the art of applied modeling in water systems is to find an appropriate balance between representativeness and applicability of a model, and that integration and leanification are two important tools for this.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and demonstrated the applicability of an ecological water system model that is sufficiently integrated and leanified for the purpose of environmental management, and which can be used to assess and predict the effects of water management on ecological systems.
the more complex the ecological system, the less complex the model should be.
we have been able to develop a new generation of ecological water system models that can be used for a wide range of environmental management purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of ecological processes and leanification can go hand-in-hand, and can be used as a basis for the application of models in environmental management.
it is possible to develop models that can be used by water managers for the management of ecological water systems, while also providing a high level of integration of ecological processes.
the integration of ecological processes can be achieved by using the most relevant and cost-effective methods for the description and simulation of the relations among variables.
